propositions: Empirical end-to-end plan-review duration (including setup, overlap detection, and post-workflow tails) exhibits p50≈339s, p90≈790s, and p99≈2524s across 78 observed complete runs; current-regime (2026-08-22 onward) shows p50≈757s and p90≈1058s across 20 runs, suggesting nonstationary performance.

Gated ticket-close (transition to in_progress with completion verification) end-to-end duration shows p50≈513s, p90≈2237s, and p99≈3607s across 38 runs; current regime shows p50≈1694s and p90≈3439s across 10 runs, with 3.8M ticket-directory visits from commit-impact scanning identified as the dominant tail source.

Inner-workflow sidecar metrics (total_ms) substantially understate operator wait time: plan omitted time (setup and post-sidecar overlap work) accounts for p50≈154s through p99≈2148s, and close omitted pre-workflow time accounts for p50≈354s through p99≈3383s.

Proposed guidance ranges derived from current-regime p50×1.20 through p90×1.20 are approximately 15–21 minutes for plan review and 34–69 minutes for gated close, distinct from the inner workflow baseline of 4–7 and 2–3 minutes respectively.

End-to-end data sourced from 78 matched plan-review and 38 matched gated-close terminal session logs (Codex JSONL) cross-referenced with provider-clean sidecar metrics (llm_calls>0, ran_model=bedrock:*) spanning 2026-08-11 through 2026-08-23; inner sidecars alone are insufficient for operator expectations.

Known limitation: 25 plan and 14 close observations are right-censored by missing terminal telemetry; current-regime p99 values are based on small samples (n=20 and n=10) and should be reported as tail evidence rather than stable SLA percentiles.
